title: DOJ vows to fast-track release of eligible PDLs aged 70 and up
summary: The Department of Justice (DOJ) on Wednesday committed to expedite the release of eligible persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) aged 70 and above as part of efforts to decongest jails.

blocks.text: Published November 25, 2026 6:51pm
The Department of Justice (DOJ) on Wednesday committed to expedite the release of eligible persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) aged 70 and above as part of efforts to decongest jails.
Budget sponsor Senator Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan said this during the Senate plenary deliberations into the proposed P44.283 billion budget of the DOJ and its attached agencies for fiscal year 2027.

“According to the good Secretary, this December 7, the Executive — Office of the President through the Deputy Executive Secretary for Legal Affairs — will be precisely discussing how to fast-track the procedure and to discuss those pending matters for release with the OP,” Pangilinan said.
This came after Senator Imee Marcos appealed to fast-track the release of PDLs who are already very old and have served their sentences for many years.
Eligibility

“Pakiusap na lamang ito na palayain ang mga lola. Dahil alam naman natin kapag 'yung PDL ay 70 years old or older and has served 10 years, 22 years, 'yung iba sa kanila higit pa, they are primarily eligible for executive clemency, hindi na regular parole,” Marcos said.

(Please just release the elderly PDLs. We know that when the PDL is 70 years old or older and has served 10 years, 22 years, some of them even more, they are primarily eligible for executive clemency, not regular parole.)

“We are all very clear that the age and the time served, the high risk status which is no longer extant even if they were convicted of a heinous crime, at that advanced age they are absolutely no threat to society,” she added.

Marcos cited Malacañang’s Memorandum Order No. 155, directing the Bureau of Corrections (BuCor), Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP), and the Board of Pardons and Parole (BPP) to immediately forward to the Office of the President records of inmates who are 70 years and above and are serving sentence by final judgment in order that the same may be considered for the purpose of extending executive clemency.

The agencies were also ordered to automatically submit names of inmates turning 70 years old and to transmit records of the said inmates to the Office of the President for review of their eligibility for executive clemency.
The senator also said the elderly PDLs could avail of the good conduct time allowance under the under Republic Act No. 10592.
Holidays

“Sana habulin na natin. December na po, Pasko na. Panahon na talaga para sa executive clemency. 'Yun lang ang hinihiling ko kasi kung tutuusin, lumalabag rin tayo sa batas sa kaka-delay nang kaka-delay,” Marcos said.

(I hope we can catch up now. It’s already December, it’s Christmas soon. It really is time for executive clemency. That is all I am asking for, because, honestly, we are actually violating the law ourselves by constantly delaying this.)

“They are really qualified and deserving. Marami sa kanila may (many of them have) terminal cancer and other illnesses — they are already wheelchair-bound, and they have families and institutions perfectly happy to take care of them,” she continued.
Citing data from DOJ, Pangilinan said the number of PDLs being released has increased since 2020.
“In 2024, halos 100% ang dumoble na ang mga releases from 2020. In 2025, about, from 57,000, they released 75,000---that's about 50% more,” the budget sponsor said.
(In 2024, the releases reached almost 100%, double the figures from 2020. In 2025, from 57,000, they released 75,000---that's about 50% more.)
“So dumadami na ang number of PDLs being released (so the number of PDLs being released is increasing). The rate has increased, but yes, they still need to do it faster,” he added. — BAP, GMA News
